STUDENTS NATIONWIDE HOLD WALKOUTS VS CORRUPTION

Universities across the country staged walkouts and protests calling for truth, accountability, and an end to corruption.

At Ateneo de Manila University, the community gathered at the Red Brick Road, with Akbayan and Kabataan Partylists joining student organizations such as the Sanggunian, League of Filipino Students–Katipunan, and Ateneo Student Catholic Action.

In Ateneo de Davao, students led by the Blue Knights for Human Rights marched at the Sunken Garden to denounce corruption and rights abuses.

At De La Salle University, students and faculty formed a human chain outside the campus and held a candlelight protest against systemic corruption.

In Bulacan, hundreds from Bulacan State University rallied from the Capitol to campus gates, carrying placards against corruption and calling out both national issues and campus concerns. Student leaders highlighted the role of youth in holding leaders accountable, while workers and educators linked the struggle to basic services and academic freedom.

At Cavite State University, students wearing black joined the Laya't Diwa protest, raising issues from corruption and budget cuts to commercialization and gender rights.

Tarlac State University's Supreme Student Council, defying restrictions on assemblies, led a lighting rally outside the CBA building, joined by progressive groups.

In Los Baños, more than 7,000 members of the UPLB community staged the school's largest walkout in six years, converging at Oblation Park. Speakers condemned plundered public funds amid worsening crises in education, jobs, and rights, launching UP Action Los Baños as a united alliance against corruption.

UP Mindanao also mobilized around 600 students, faculty, and staff in a university-wide walkout decrying corruption and education budget cuts.
